sample_unit: queries (200 dental radiographs, 12 landmarks, 3 repetitions; 10,800 API calls)

links.outcome: MLLM landmark localisation versus fourth-year dental student consensus on same radiographs
links.effect: Both models remained inferior to student consensus on all periapical and panoramic comparisons; GPT-5.4 matched students only on cephalometric landmarks; Gemini approached parity only on cephalometric points under guided prompting.
links.quote: Both models remained inferior to the student consensus on all periapical and panoramic comparisons, with Gemini 3.1 Pro approaching parity only on cephalometric points under guided prompting.

links.outcome: Model behavior variation under different prompting and repeated runs
links.effect: Guided prompting had heterogeneous effects, improving some landmarks and severely regressing others; GPT-5.4 sent most lower-left canine apex predictions to the wrong lower-right molar region, a prompt-resistant pattern absent in Gemini.
links.quote: Guided prompting produced heterogeneous effects, improving localisation of some landmarks while causing severe regression on others; most notably, GPT-5.4 directed the majority of lower-left canine apex predictions to the incorrect lower-right molar region, a prompt-resistant mislocalisation pattern absent in Gemini 3.1 Pro.

unlisted_practices: Grid-based coordinate framework for benchmarking spatial landmark localisation of multimodal LLMs on dental radiographs

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates multimodal LLMs against human dental student consensus on dental radiograph landmark identification and tests guided prompting versus zero-shot prompting as a prompt guardrail/strategy.
